description: An authored research taxonomy of user-facing AI software workflows. It is not a census, capability assertion, product ranking, source-use approval or adopted change to frozen builder contract v1.

classification_policy.primary_category: Choose one main user workflow per product or independently identifiable module; additional supported workflows receive secondary category tags.
classification_policy.multi_label: Category membership is many-to-many; overlapping counts must not be added as distinct product totals.
classification_policy.subcategory_rule: Subcategories are research territories, not claims that any named product covers them.
classification_policy.facet_rule: Facet values describe one evidenced offering or claim scope; unknown remains unknown.
classification_policy.ai_involvement: Require evidence of a material AI-assisted workflow; vendor use of the word AI is a discovery signal only.
classification_policy.scope_growth: Add or split a category only for a distinct user decision, evidence method or independently maintainable workflow; record taxonomy version and migration.

categories.name: General assistants and answer search

categories.inclusion_rule: Include an identifiable software product, independently discoverable product module, or software-delivered service that offers an AI-assisted end-user workflow within this definition; record the evidence for AI involvement.

language_coverage.shape: repeatable language/dialect/direction records with claim evidence
language_coverage.no_inference: Interface language, input language and output-quality evidence are distinct.

geography.shape: repeatable country/region/jurisdiction and offering scope with dates
geography.no_inference: Website access does not establish account, purchasing or lawful-use availability.

accessibility.shape: claim records for supported interaction needs, standards versions and independent tests
accessibility.no_inference: A vendor accessibility statement is not an independent conformance test.

enterprise_controls.shape: claim records for authentication, authorization, tenancy, audit, retention, training-use and residency
enterprise_controls.no_inference: Enterprise plan naming is not proof of any control.

global_exclusions: Foundation models, model releases, provider inference routes, accelerators, inference engines and generic infrastructure are owned by existing T0–T6 research; cross-link rather than clone.
Pure libraries, SDKs, frameworks, protocols and connectors are excluded unless a distinct usable application product or application module can be identified.
AI consultancy and implementation agencies without an identifiable software-delivered workflow remain service-provider notes, outside application counts.
Directories, papers, datasets and benchmark results are sources or linked entities; their existence does not make them end-user applications.
Announcements, demos, abandoned products and unconfirmed AI features remain labeled candidate notes; they do not automatically become active product records.
No automatic copying of marketplace listings, logos, screenshots, reviews, terms or source databases without an eligible source-use decision.

boundary_cases.territory: AI evaluation, model-operations and observability consoles
boundary_cases.rule: Admit only a distinct user-facing software product/workflow; link component evaluation, monitoring and runtime records to existing T6/T2 owners.

boundary_cases.territory: Data labeling, synthetic-data creation and dataset curation workbenches
boundary_cases.rule: Application workflow is in scope; resulting datasets, licenses and evaluation corpora remain separate dataset entities and rights decisions.
A usable builder is a product; a framework/library remains T4. A marketplace is initially a discovery source, and every listed bot requires its own identity and scope decision.

boundary_cases.territory: Specialist mathematics, physics, chemistry and engineering workbenches
boundary_cases.rule: Classify by actual user workflow and scientific domain; keep a model or paper distinct from an application and retain unvalidated outputs as such.

boundary_cases.territory: Content provenance, detection, moderation and authenticity tools
boundary_cases.rule: Classify by editorial, trust, governance or community workflow; detection performance and certification require explicit scoped evidence.

boundary_cases.territory: Language, geography, mobile, browser, local/offline and accessibility variants
boundary_cases.rule: Use orthogonal facets and offering identities. Do not create a duplicate product per language, platform or region absent an independent product identity.

boundary_cases.territory: Fashion, beauty, hobbies, dating, religion and other specialist consumer workflows
boundary_cases.rule: Use relevant creative, shopping, wellness, lifestyle or social scope; record unexamined subdomains and propose a versioned category split if the user decision warrants independent maintenance.

boundary_cases.territory: Software-delivered professional services and managed work products
boundary_cases.rule: Include identifiable software-delivered workflows with an operator and offering; preserve human service versus software automation evidence. Pure consultancy without such a workflow is outside product counts.
